body:
# Critterweight 0.9.17

This preview overhauls the commentary booth, gives the whole playable roster a new look with
expressions and moving parts, and redraws every fighter's abilities. Combat itself is unchanged:
timing, damage, reach, collision bodies, physics and stats are exactly as in 0.9.16.

## Highlights

- **Commentary that follows the fight.** The booth now decides what to talk about from what is
  actually happening: knockouts, referee stoppages, judges' decisions and round results each have
  their own calls, every fighter's abilities are called by name (and whether they landed), and quiet
  stretches get observations about pressure, momentum, the clock or a fighter who is hurt before
  any joke. Calls expire if they would arrive late, the big moment always wins, and nothing is said
  that the fight contradicts (no ropes or corner crews in a cage, no fence jokes without a fence).
- **Far less repetition.** The booth remembers what you have heard across rematches, Career bouts
  and game restarts, prefers lines you have not heard, and spaces out running jokes.
- **337 new commentary lines and 7 corrected ones**, recorded with the same three voices in 521
  clips, including whole-sentence takes with the roster's names and ceremonial winner calls; after a
  technical check of every clip, 19 were re-recorded where the audio was cut off, flat, rushed or
  paused oddly. 59 older lines that got facts wrong were retired. Speech still works fully offline.
- **New art for all eight fighters.** Stoke, Dredge, Gusto, Dozer, Slurry, Jitters, Varga and Knell
  were rebuilt with new forms, faces and details, readable from the fight camera: Stoke's riveted
  boiler and back stacks, Dredge's barnacled plates and mooring chain, Slurry's fin and glowing
  pores, Jitters' battery-jelly bell and tentacles, Knell's haunted diving suit and lantern, Varga's
  new fighter build, and more. Eyes look at the opponent and blink, brows and jaws react to the
  fight, and crests, fins, chains, tentacles, hoses and hair swing with the motion. A new finish
  gives cloth, metal, shells, jelly and ghostly surfaces their own look.
- **Legacy Varga skin** (Settings › Graphics): brings back Varga's original look from before this
  update. It is your own preference: it applies everywhere you see him (fighter select, matches,
  practice, Career, spectating, online, the hub), other players see their own choice, and he fights
  exactly the same either way.
- **New ability effects for every fighter.** Abilities, JUICE, charged heavies, projectiles, ground
  effects, elemental hits and reactions now have a build-up, a strike, motion and a fade, in each
  fighter's style: Stoke's steam jets and furnace blasts, Dredge's tides and whirlpools, Gusto's
  vortices, Dozer's dust and rock spires, Slurry's sludge, Jitters' lightning, Knell's ghostly bell
  and lantern, and Varga's crisp gold impacts. Every area effect now shows its true shape and
  reach on the floor (a cone is drawn as that cone), the effects read on bright and dark floors,
  and they respect the Effects quality and Reduce flashing settings. The hub shows your fighter's
  ability effects too.

## Verification

The commentary was audited before and after the overhaul: the same twelve seeded bouts and two
scripted sequences, played in real time across a game restart on 0.9.16 and on this build. The booth
used 338 different lines instead of 125, exact repeats within a bout fell from 137 to 15 (and from 106
to 7 across rematches), the referee stoppage was called as a stoppage rather than a knockout, and it
talked slightly more often than before (10.8 lines a minute instead of 9.5). The new art and effects
were captured and compared shot by shot against 0.9.16, and saves from 0.9.16 load and continue. Nothing here has been listened to or
playtested by a person yet, so please report anything that sounds or looks off.

# Critterweight 0.9.16

This preview adds a persistent fighter Career recreated from Cage Rules' career, optional 10-point must scoring and a referee for the standard duel, and a built-in Cage Rules rules preset. Critterweight's own combat stays as it is: there is no grappling, ground game or submissions, and grabs keep their simple throw-and-escape layer.

## Highlights

- **Career** (Campaign › Career, now first in the Campaign menu): build one fighter over many bouts. Pick any playable fighter, a ring name, a nickname and a difficulty, then train one of six stats each week (Stamina, Chin, Speed, Power, Clinch, Defence) or rest to heal. Each week brings two or three fight offers from nine promotions in four tiers, each showing the opponent's record and rating, a danger tag, the purse and the win bonus. Wins raise popularity and open bigger promotions; at the top a five-round title shot waits, and champions defend the belt. Purses buy gym upgrades, and injuries heal over the weeks. Records, standing, fight history and a news log are kept for every career. Three save slots per profile save after every action, and Retire moves a save aside instead of deleting it.
- **10-point scoring** (Rules Editor › Scoring): fighters cannot be knocked out by damage, so the HP bars disappear. Every round is fought, and three judges (Even card, Volume, Impact) score each one 10-9, 10-10 or 10-8 from damage, clean strikes, knockdowns, throws, ring-outs, parries and guard breaks. The HUD shows the round and each judge's running total, a scorecard appears between rounds, and the results screen shows every card. A drawn decision follows the Sudden death setting.
- **Referee** (Rules Editor › Referee, works with either scoring): nobody can hit a fighter who is down. The referee counts strike knockdowns, waves a fighter up after four seconds (you can get up sooner, and staying down recovers stamina faster) and stops the fight after five knockdowns in one round. Jeremy's original Cage Rules referee is imported through the Cage Rules asset tools: he keeps his distance during the action, holds the attacker back, waves off stoppages and raises the winner's arm. Online players see the same referee.
- **Cage Rules preset**: the Standard Duel with 10-point scoring and the referee on, available wherever rules presets are listed. Career bouts use it with three rounds (five for title fights) and allow draws.
- The in-game patch notes now include v0.9.15, which the previous build was missing.

## Verification

The full source suite on the release commit completed 862 tests: 861 passed, zero failed, and one graphical-audio test was skipped because the suite runs without the graphical audio backend. All 437 scripts compile. Against the exported Windows game, 96 headless and 26 rendered tests covering 10-point scoring, the referee, the Career, rules presets, snapshots and recorded speech passed with no skips. The release script also runs a fresh script check, boots the game to the title screen and passes the 20 rendered playtest regressions.

The judges' thresholds, the referee's five-knockdown limit and the Career's injury and fight-of-the-night numbers were calibrated on 52 headless bot duels (DECISIONS D-045). Online behaviour was checked over loopback only, and no physical-controller or human playtest has been done yet, so please report anything that feels off in play, especially the judging of close rounds and the Career economy.
title: Critterweight 0.9.16

body:
# Critterweight 0.9.15

This combined preview release brings together the v0.9.15 playtest work, including the campaign and editor improvements, new fighters, expanded recorded commentary, and the community soundtrack additions.

## Highlights

- Adds Varga, a Fighting-style martial artist with a deeper move set and controller support, and Knell, a Spectral fighter with a standard control scheme. Both have abilities, campaign upgrades, and Compendium entries.
- Adds the editor-only Rooftop Canvas arena layout, letting custom arenas use a configurable square or rectangular floor bounded by rooftop edges.
- Improves campaign progression and run resumption, route-map presentation and event art, combat announcements and fight HUD, controller navigation, arena editing, and fighter selection.
- Adds 854 new Devon/Kendall announcer takes, alongside the recorded coach dialogue and player-name variants, for more varied calls and longer booth conversations.
- Adds eight community music tracks and a Jukebox for choosing ordered, shuffled, or repeating playlists. Audio credits and license details are included in-game and in the bundled documentation.
- Includes the previously playtested v0.9.15 fixes, including the saved monitor choice, quieter single menu-navigation sound, patch notes, inverted spectator camera option, and controller-friendly menus.

## Verification

The combined source suite completed 775 tests: 774 passed, zero failed, and one graphical-audio test was skipped because the suite ran without the graphical audio backend. The packaged combined preview completed 72 checks: 70 passed, zero failed, and two source-only checks were skipped. All 406 scripts compiled successfully.

The packaged checks cover the recorded speech and music bank, announcer behavior, both new fighters, the v0.9.15 regressions, arena canvas, UI focus, and layout. The release packaging script also runs a fresh script check and boots the tagged Windows game to the title screen. The automated suite confirms technical integration; please continue to report any issues found during play.

See [the combined verification summary](../evidence/verification/v0.9.15-combined/summary.json) and [the full playtest report](../evidence/verification/v0.9.15-combined/summary.json) for details.
title: Critterweight 0.9.15

# Critterweight 0.9.13

This preview adds free, licensed audio replacements and makes Random available anywhere a fighter is selected.

## Audio

- Replaces title/poster music with Funkorama, Cannery radio with Backbay Lounge, both combat slots with Furious Freak, and boss music with Volatile Reaction. The finished recordings use no mismatched generated stems; boss JUICE still jumps to section B.
- Adds Kenney CC0 result jingles, punch/impact and guard sounds, surface footsteps, menu feedback, and book/coin UI cues.
- Adds CC0 crowd ambience/applause and quiet dock water. Freesound crowd clips were skipped because their download requires an account; a public CC0 OpenGameArt source was used instead.
- No paid version is included. Kevin MacLeod tracks are CC BY 4.0 and require the attribution in Credits; the other installed clips are CC0 1.0. Full provenance and SHA-256 list: docs/audio/replacement-audio-inventory.txt.
- Named creature calls and custom announcer/coach lines remain generated so their identities and written performances stay intact.
- The imported bank passes Godot import, runtime validation and asset-hash checks. Please audition the music in-game; automated checks confirm technical integration, not sound quality.

## Fighter selection

Every fighter picker now includes Random, including campaign/Fight Camp, Bookie, versus, multiplayer lobby, AI Lab, Cannery sparring and the locker. A random choice resolves to a concrete fighter before a fight or campaign run is created.

## Verification

See docs/evidence/verification/v0.9.13/README.md for the exact source and packaged test results, build manifest, boot report and release asset hashes.
title: Critterweight 0.9.13

body:
# Critterweight 0.9.12

Fixes and additions from the 0.9.11 playtest.

## Campaigns and watching fights

- Escape and the Back prompt leave the campaign lobby correctly.
- A completed campaign fight opens its reward/next decision and saves that state. Resume restores the pending reward, event, shop, rest or route map. An unfinished fight still restarts when resumed.
- If a v0.9.11 save still marks the first fight as unfinished, it will replay that fight once: the old bug never saved its completed result. Subsequent wins advance and save normally.
- Controller navigation connects the suspended-run buttons to the Bookie's Table and the new-run form.
- The Bookie's Table shows the live 3D fights, with 1–4x playback. Skip ahead runs the same fight at 8x; Watch returns to it immediately.
- Spectate cycles through Follow, Locked and Free cameras. Free flight uses LS/WASD to move, RS/right-drag to look, A/Space to rise and LT/Shift to descend. The Bookie's free view uses View/Tab to switch between flying and the table controls.

## Menus, Compendium and controls

- The main menu keeps its poster design with eight groups and no scrolling. Tutorial is under Fight; AI Lab and Mods are under Create; Controls and Credits are under Settings.
- Submenus stay open when the mouse moves toward their options or away from the left column.
- New Compendium: inspect the fighters' actual 3D models, stats, abilities and cooldowns; browse elements and reactions, arenas, game rules, field objects and a practical guide.
- Right-stick scrolling is shared across focused information panels, text and lists. Focused rows scroll far enough to show their bottom outline.
- The new-rules picker uses a grid that fits the screen.
- Arena Editor map focus keeps the sticks controlling the map. View switches back to the panels; Palette and Details can each be hidden. Toolbar and control hints wrap cleanly, including after an input-device switch.
- Dialogue uses your profile name, with Rookie replacing the old default You. Rename it in Profile.
- Ability names now accompany their HUD bindings. RB works for all six playable fighters: many second abilities are a buff, counter, hover, cloud, dive or placed pad rather than a projectile. The Compendium explains each one.

## The Cannery

- Chum Cannon offers Warm-up, Pressure and Homing hell. Harder settings fire faster, predict movement and, at the highest level, track early in flight while leaving a final dodge window.
- Crate Toss calls for near/middle/far targets with bonuses and streaks. Throw strength matters; one repeated full heave is no longer the best strategy. Used crates cannot score twice, and all crates reset after the game.
- Walls block crate pickups. Movement direction follows the visible camera throughout room transitions.
- Needles' price board clearly identifies itself as a preview. It explains that purchases and services are available at campaign Shop nodes, what each service does, and the difference between Scrip and Clout.

## Settings and audio

- Resolution is a dropdown: select the desired mode once, then Keep/Revert once.
- Show FPS displays a counter above menus and fights.
- Opening an AI Lab dropdown keeps the music playing; owned popup windows count as application focus.
- Removed continuous buzz/hum layers from eight ambience loops and repaired overlapping ambience fades.
- FSR options now say they work across GPU vendors, including NVIDIA. Godot 4.5.1's stock renderer does not expose DLSS, so this release does not add a DLSS option.
- [Complete generated-audio inventory and stock replacement shortlist](https://github.com/adambennett/PokeMMA/blob/v0.9.12/docs/audio/REPLACEMENT_GUIDE.md), with individual filenames, source links and license notes. Proposed stock assets are not installed in this release.

Verification: the full source suite ran 711 tests (710 passed, no failures, one graphical-only skip); all 20 playtest regressions passed in the rendered Windows export. The tagged build checked all 391 scripts, reached the title in 4.5 seconds and passed all 20 rendered regressions. All seven uploaded asset sizes and SHA-256 digests match the local release files.

Details, including full-suite-only engine warnings and the clean rendered/exported runs, are recorded in [the playtest fix report](https://github.com/adambennett/PokeMMA/blob/842b4056ef0857464a4f3aad0231810908e6f561/docs/evidence/verification/v0.9.12/README.md). The release remains a 0.9.x preview. Windows and Linux game/server packages are provided; Linux gameplay and physical-controller testing are not claimed by the automated Windows checks.
title: Critterweight 0.9.12

body:
**Preview build** of Critterweight for the playtest week. It is 0.9.10 with **combat that you can feel** and a camera that walls can't block.

## Play it
- **Download `Critterweight-0.9.11-windows-x64.exe`** and double-click it: the whole game in one file. Or get `Critterweight-0.9.11-windows-x64.zip`, the same game plus the player guide, modding guide and licences.
- Windows 10/11 64-bit with a Vulkan-capable GPU. An Xbox-style controller is recommended; keyboard and mouse work everywhere.
- Not code-signed: if SmartScreen says "Windows protected your PC", choose **More info → Run anyway**.
- Saves live in `%APPDATA%\Critterweight` and carry over from 0.9.x. The main menu footer shows the version and commit for bug reports.

## New since 0.9.10
- **Landing a hit feels like it.**
  - Offline fights freeze for a split second when your hits land or you get hit (longer on counters), and on every KO. Online fights never pause.
  - Your hits zoom-punch and shake the camera, with bigger sparks, a stronger flash and stronger controller rumble. The fighter who is hit jolts. The camera-shake setting still scales all of this.
  - The chunk a hit takes off stays lit on the health bar for a moment before it drains.
- **Walls no longer hide the fight.** Pit walls, posts, props and scenery between the camera and the fighters fade to see-through, and crowd figures in the way shrink out of the shot.
- Gameplay itself is unchanged: same moves, damage, bots and balance.

## Known gaps in this preview
- **Mashed attacks still miss often** against a bot that moves well (15-41 % land). Making attacks home in on a nearby opponent is a separate, measured change for later.
- **Online play has only been tested on one PC.** Both ends must run 0.9.11. Playing across the internet needs the host's UDP port (default 7777) forwarded.
- **The Journeyman bot still loses most bouts to pure button-mashing.**
- **Some fighter matchups are lopsided.** Dredge still loses almost every bout to Slurry between bots.
- **The Linux game itself has not been run** (only the Linux server), and nothing has run on a real Steam Deck.

Files:
- Windows game: `.exe`, `.zip`;
- dedicated servers: `-server-windows-x64.zip`, `-server-linux-x86_64.tar.gz`;
- Linux game: `-linux-x86_64.tar.gz`;
- `BUILD_MANIFEST.json`, `SHA256SUMS.txt`.
title: Critterweight 0.9.11

**Preview build** of Critterweight for the playtest week. It is 0.9.9 with the **new creature art**: the twelve combat creatures were remodelled in Blender. This is the art from the `-alt` comparison builds, which are now retired.

## Play it
- **Download `Critterweight-0.9.10-windows-x64.exe`** and double-click it: the whole game in one file. Or get `Critterweight-0.9.10-windows-x64.zip`, the same game plus the player guide, modding guide and licences.

## New since 0.9.9
- **New creature art.** The six fighters, the three bosses (Bilge, Conduit, Snappington) and the three minion types (Scrapling, Blister, Kid Lamprey) have new models.
  - Clearer faces, cleaner colours without the blotchy paint, jointed limbs and tidier signature details.
  - Gameplay is unchanged: every hitbox, move and stat is the same, so the shapes match the old ones. In a fight you mostly see the fighters' backs, so the change shows most up close.
  - The models are about 40 % smaller on disk. Busy scenes ran no slower in desktop benchmarks.
- The in-game credits list the art revamp.

## Known gaps in this preview

- **Some fighter matchups are lopsided.** Dredge still loses almost every bout to Slurry between bots.
- **Mashing Light doesn't always land a fighter's whole string.**
- **The Linux game itself has not been run** (only the Linux server), and nothing has run on a real Steam Deck.
- The eight hub characters and the two crowd fans keep their original models.

body:
**Alt build, for comparison:** Critterweight 0.9.9 with the **revamped creature art**, built from the main 0.9.9 plus the creature art pull request ([#1](https://github.com/adambennett/PokeMMA/pull/1)). Everything else is identical to 0.9.9. Play both and decide which art the game keeps; nothing is merged into the main line until you choose.

## Play it
- **Download `Critterweight-0.9.9-alt.1-windows-x64.exe`** and double-click it, or get the `.zip`. It can sit beside the 0.9.9 build.
- Both builds use the same saves in `%APPDATA%\Critterweight`, so you can switch between them freely.
- **Online:** an alt build only plays with the same alt build, not with 0.9.9, because both ends must run the same version.
- Not code-signed: if SmartScreen says "Windows protected your PC", choose **More info → Run anyway**.

## What is different from 0.9.9
- **New models for twelve creatures:** the six fighters (Stoke, Jitters, Dredge, Slurry, Gusto, Dozer), the three bosses (Bilge, Conduit, Snappington) and the three minion families.
  - They were remodelled in Blender from new concept sheets: slimmer joints, cleaner colour blocks, clearer eyes and faces, signature props.
  - The models total 4.7 MB (8.1 MB before) and 14 % fewer triangles. A desktop bench shows no slowdown.
- **Unchanged:** the fighters' bodies, moves, timings and balance are exactly the same. Only the look changed. Hub characters and the crowd keep their current art.
- Before and after images for every creature: [the evidence gallery](https://github.com/adambennett/PokeMMA/blob/art/creature-revamp/docs/evidence/art/revamp/README.md).

## Known gaps
The same as 0.9.9 (see its release notes). Also:
- The art hasn't been checked on a real Steam Deck.
- Not every move has been checked against the new meshes.
- In busy 8-fighter scenes at Deck resolution, the cage's foreground posts and the bottom HUD can hide fighters. That's a camera/UI follow-up, not part of this art.
title: Critterweight 0.9.9-alt.1 (alt build, for comparison)

body:
**Preview build** of Critterweight for the playtest week. It is 0.9.7 plus a fix that lets the Linux dedicated server host Windows players. The remaining release-candidate work is listed under *Known gaps*.

## Play it
- **Download `Critterweight-0.9.8-windows-x64.exe`** and double-click it: the whole game in one file. Or get `Critterweight-0.9.8-windows-x64.zip`, the same game plus the player guide, modding guide and licences.
- Windows 10/11 64-bit with a Vulkan-capable GPU. An Xbox-style controller is recommended; keyboard and mouse work everywhere.
- Not code-signed: if SmartScreen says "Windows protected your PC", choose **More info → Run anyway**.
- Start with **Tutorial**, then **Fight**. Saves live in `%APPDATA%\Critterweight` and carry over from 0.9.x. The main menu footer shows the version and commit for bug reports.

## New since 0.9.7
- **The Linux dedicated server works with Windows players.** The Linux server package ran for the first time, in a Debian 12 container. Windows clients could join it, but every match was refused with "Your copy of arena … differs from the host's".
  - The cause: Linux and Windows wrote the same decimal numbers differently when the game computed content checksums.
  - Checksums now use the exact number values, so both platforms agree. A full duel then played to the end at 30 updates/s.
  - The same fix keeps saves and online party runs consistent between platforms, for example a save copied to a Steam Deck. Saves from earlier versions still load.
- **Docker:** the server guide now says how to run the Linux server in a container (`docker run --init`).
- **Support:** `Critterweight.exe --headless -- --arena-hash <arena id>` prints an arena's content hash, to compare two installations.

## In 0.9.7
- **The Bookie's Table: camera presets** (Broadcast, Director, Free) during fights. The control bar no longer hides the fighters' health-plate details.

## In 0.9.6
- **Chum Rush** supplement picks apply. **Chumball** knockouts no longer count as goals. The **Rooftop** railings guard the edges instead of fencing the arena in half. **Bots** walk around props.

## Known gaps in this preview
- **Online play has only been tested on one PC.** Windows to Windows uses loopback, and Linux server to Windows clients goes through a container on the same PC.
  - Playing across the internet needs the host's UDP port (default 7777) forwarded.
  - Play online with others on 0.9.8: both ends must run the same version.
- **The Journeyman bot still loses most bouts to pure button-mashing.** The target is about even.
- **Some fighter matchups are lopsided.** Dredge still loses almost every bout to Slurry between bots. The balance pass is pending.
- **Mashing Light doesn't always land a fighter's whole string,** because knockback can push the target out of reach. Tuning is pending.

body:
**Preview build** of Critterweight for the playtest week. It is 0.9.1 plus tougher top bots, a combat fix and a much lighter dedicated server. The remaining release-candidate work is listed under *Known gaps*.

## Play it
- **Download `Critterweight-0.9.2-windows-x64.exe`** and double-click it: the whole game in one file. Or get `Critterweight-0.9.2-windows-x64.zip`, the same game plus the player guide, modding guide and licences.

## New since 0.9.1
- **Top bots beat button-mashing.** In our tests against a pure masher, each tier played 24 mirror bouts across all six fighters:
  - the Headliner wins 17 of 24 (was 12);
  - the Hall-of-Famer wins 20 of 24 (was 17);
  - the Punching Bag still loses almost every bout, so new players can still win by mashing.

  How they do it:
  - they learn during a fight how much gap a string really leaves before hitting back;
  - they learn their own ranges faster;
  - they read an opponent walking in;
  - they keep the guard up through a stream of attacks instead of raising it afresh for every hit.

  The Journeyman and Contender read a little better too.
- **Combat fix:** a burst at the attacker's own body, such as Dozer's Hoof Stomp, can now be blocked by guarding toward him. At point blank it used to hit through a front guard.
- **Dedicated server:**
  - An 8-fighter server now uses about 30 % of one core, was about 45 %. An idle one uses almost nothing. Godot's frame limiter busy-waited on Windows; the server now paces itself, and it runs one physics worker thread.
  - Server output is flushed line by line, so service managers and log files see it at once.
- The packaged-build test failures from the 0.9.1 verification are fixed. They were test-harness issues, not game bugs, and all 21 tests pass inside a fresh package.

- **Online play has only been tested on one PC (loopback).**

title: Critterweight 0.9.1

body:
**Preview build** of Critterweight, a physical creature cage-fighting game. This is a test build from the release-candidate work in progress: everything below is playable, and the remaining work is listed under *Known gaps*.

## Play it
- **Download `Critterweight-0.9.0-windows-x64.exe`** and double-click it. That single file is the whole game. Or get `Critterweight-0.9.0-windows-x64.zip` (same game plus the player guide, modding guide and licences).
- Windows 10/11 64-bit with a Vulkan-capable GPU. An Xbox-style controller is recommended; keyboard and mouse work everywhere.
- The build is not code-signed. If Windows SmartScreen says "Windows protected your PC", choose **More info → Run anyway**.
- Start with **Tutorial** (Granny Haymaker's ten short lessons), then **Fight**. Controls: in-game *Controls* screen, or `PLAYER_GUIDE.md` in the zip.
- Saves and settings live in `%APPDATA%\Critterweight`, so newer builds keep your progress. The version and commit are in the main menu's footer: please quote them in bug reports.

## What's in it
- Six fighters with full kits (Stoke, Dredge, Gusto, Dozer, Slurry, Jitters), real active-ragdoll combat, six elements with reactions.
- Versus, Practice, Spectate (auto-director), Tutorial; bonus modes Spotlight Hog, Chumball, Absolute Unit, Chum Rush; Tag Team.
- Campaigns: **Off the Street** (fresh runs) and **Fight Camp** (permanent upgrades, explore The Cannery hub), The Dosage ladder, **The Bookie's Table** autobattler; bosses Bilge, Conduit and Snappington.
- Rules editor and arena editor (save, share, test-play); local mods (three example mods included); the **AI Lab** (train your own fighter AI locally: evolution strategies and behaviour cloning) with sample policies for every fighter.
- Online: host or join by address or LAN (default UDP port 7777), lobby with ready/teams/voting, dedicated server package for Windows and Linux.

## Known gaps in this preview
- **Online co-op campaign runs** currently sync only the route votes; fights, shops and events in an online party run are being wired up. Local and online versus play work.
- Bot difficulty tuning and the roster balance pass are in progress (some matchups are lopsided; the top bot tier can still be beaten by button-mashing).
- The Linux packages are built and checked for portability but have not been run on Linux hardware yet.
- The 8-fighter dedicated server uses more CPU than our target; optimization is pending.
- Online play has only been tested on one PC (loopback); playing across the internet needs the host's port forwarded.

Files: the Windows game (`.exe` and `.zip`), the dedicated servers (`-server-windows-x64.zip`, `-server-linux-x86_64.tar.gz`), the Linux game (`-linux-x86_64.tar.gz`), `BUILD_MANIFEST.json` and `SHA256SUMS.txt`.
